text: marta: quick sync — we need to lock down the reranker endpoint response shape before the console rollout. current questions: normalized vs raw scores, per-candidate cost accounting, and pagination semantics. cc @alex for API, @kevin for routing/quota.
_thread:
alex: +1. from API POV I'd prefer a deterministic envelope we can version. proposal: `candidates: [{id, text, score, raw_logit?, model, model_units}]`, plus a `summary` with chosen_model and timing. makes it easy for console and telemetry.
kevin: question — do we expose model_units to customers? that leaks internal cost. maybe expose a coarse `cost_tier: low|medium|high` instead and keep units internal for billing.
marta: I think exposing cost_tier is reasonable. but platform needs per-candidate accounting for routing/quotas. i'd like the routing decision to be able to use `score` vs `raw_logit` depending on model family. need a clear contract: `score` must be normalized to [0,1] and `raw_logit` optional and opaque.
shyam: for fallback behavior we should include a `fallback_chain` field at response-level when we hit cheaper model fallbacks, e.g. `fallback_chain: ["model-3b-slim","model-1b-fallback"]` so we can debug quality regressions.
alex: +1 to normalized score. but normalization rules must be explicit: per-model min/max or softmax across candidates? we should avoid cross-request softmax because it breaks pagination. propose per-candidate sigmoid normalization derived from training calibration, and document "use for ranking display only".
kevin: quotas — customers are charged per-candidate score unit. we need to decide if pagination counts are charged per-request vs per-candidate returned. billing prefers per-candidate considered (including candidates filtered out by server-side heuristics). customers expect per-returned-candidate billing.
marta: tradeoff. If we charge per-returned-candidate, users can request huge `max_candidates` and game it. We should cap `max_candidates` and count against quota the number of candidates evaluated (server-side). Add `evaluated_candidates` to telemetry and `returned_candidates` to response.
shyam: UI/console needs telemetry metrics: p50/p95 latency per model, average evaluated_candidates, cache hit rate for prefix-KV, and score distribution histograms. Also show rollback button when a rollout increases evaluated_candidates > baseline by X%.
alex: rollout UX — we should surface a preview mode that returns `debug=true` bundle to admins with `raw_logit` and `evaluated_candidates` but not for regular keys. Also add rollout flags to the response envelope: `served_by: model-uuid`, `policy: canary|ab_test|stable`.
marta: example envelope (suggested):
```
{
  "summary": {
    "served_by": "model-3b-v4",
    "policy": "canary",
    "evaluated_candidates": 48,
    "returned_candidates": 10
  },
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1","text": "...","score": 0.87, "raw_logit": -0.25, "model": "model-3b-v4", "cost_tier": "medium"},
    {"id": "c2","text": "...","score": 0.45, "model": "model-1b-fallback", "cost_tier": "low"}
  ]
}
```
kevin: looks good. on quotas we should document billing: "quota units consumed = sum(model_consume_map[model]*evaluated_candidates_for_model)" and expose only `cost_tier` publicly.
deploy-bot: deploy status: reranker-v2 schema branch passed unit + integration tests on staging, rollout gated behind feature-flag `rerank_v2_envelope`.
marta: action items: 1) alex to draft API spec with normalization rules and debug flag. 2) kevin to propose quota counting semantics and cap defaults (suggested cap 50). 3) shyam to list console telemetry panels + rollback thresholds. Aim to merge spec by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
alex: I’ll put a PR up with the spec and example responses, will include the sigmoid-normalization appendix.
kevin: I’ll draft the quota doc and add tests for evaluated vs returned counters.
shyam: will sketch console mockups for the new metrics and a rollback CTA.
marta: thanks — syncing with product later to align rollout messaging.
